extracted.intended_audience: UCSF biomedical researchers and grant applicants (PIs, postdocs, early-stage investigators) preparing NIH proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and internal review standards for drafting competitive NIH-style grant applications (Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigator/Environment, budget/timeline) aimed at UCSF biomedical investigators preparing submissions and resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-style scoring (1-9) / Mock review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Mock review committees provide faculty review of full applications using NIH-style numeric scoring (1-9), produce a written summary of strengths and weaknesses, and hold a discussion meeting with the PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow 4–6 weeks lead time before the deadline for mock review. Expect written critiques and a discussion to inform revisions; OSR mock reviews emulate NIH scoring and written feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should follow a four-paragraph Russell–Morrison structure, fit on one page, and present a clear visual hierarchy with the aims bolded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterate the Specific Aims 10+ times; include a conceptual figure where helpful; end with a closing impact statement. Use peer review and senior faculty polishing sessions to refine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Aims must be clear, well-structured, hypothesis-driven, and immediately convey what will be tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops and peer feedback rounds focus on clarity; the mock review looks specifically at Specific Aims clarity and structure as a primary determinant of competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims should be explicitly hypothesis-driven rather than purely descriptive or exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the hypothesis clearly in the Aims and ensure subsequent sections (Approach, Expected Outcomes) flow from and test that hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim independence (no failure cascade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims should be independent so that the failure of one aim does not cause the entire proposal to fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims so each produces interpretable results on its own; avoid co-dependent experiments or single critical-path steps that make other aims contingent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data sufficiency (quantitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quantitative preliminary data that credibly support the feasibility of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mock reviewers favor quantitative evidence; present data clearly and relate it directly to the aims to demonstrate feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan with power calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear statistical analysis plan that includes power calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report power calculations and assumptions; reviewers expect explicit statistical methods tied to outcomes and sample size justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification with citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify sample sizes with appropriate citations and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant literature or pilot data to justify sample sizes; connect justification to the power analysis and expected effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicates and reagent authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify biological and technical replicates and describe authentication of cell lines and antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document planned replicates, authentication procedures, and other measures (e.g., cell-line validation) to satisfy rigor and reproducibility expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a biological variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Address sex as a biological variable where relevant in experimental design and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for sex-balanced sampling or justify exclusions; specify analyses to detect sex-based effects when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-aim Approach components (Rationale, Approach, Expected Outcomes, Pitfalls, Alternatives, Rigor)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each aim explicitly state the rationale, detailed approach, expected outcomes, potential pitfalls, alternative strategies, and rigor considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for this structured per-aim layout; including explicit pitfalls and alternatives demonstrates feasibility and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must be described with sufficient specificity to convince reviewers the work is doable and rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague method descriptions; give enough procedural detail, references for techniques, and links to cores/consultants where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor language explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly include language and elements that address rigor (blinding, randomization, controls, reproducibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make rigor practices explicit rather than implied; mock reviewers expect clear statements about how bias will be minimized and results validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator productivity and fit for career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate investigator productivity proportionate to career stage and appropriate independence for the role (especially for ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame publication record and contributions relative to career stage; for early-stage investigators provide an explicit independence narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named collaborators and specific roles
rubrics_metrics.description: List specific collaborators by name and clearly define their roles and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters and text should indicate concrete commitments and specific expertise, not generic statements of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment & institutional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate an enabling environment by citing specific institutional cores, disease centers, training programs, and clinical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name UCSF cores (genomics, imaging, biostatistics, etc.), training programs (PSTP, MSTP), and clinical integrations that will support the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support must be specific about the collaborator/contributor role rather than generic endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers penalize generic letters; letters should describe resources, commitment level, and concrete support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets must be realistic, justified, and not padded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic cost estimates and justify major line items; mock reviewers will ding inflated or poorly justified budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline realism and internal submission milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a realistic timeline for project milestones and follow an internal pre-submission schedule (e.g., 6 months: Specific Aims draft; 4 months: full draft + mock review; 2 months: revisions; 1 month: polish; submit >1 week early).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the internal timeline to allow for iterative review; reviewers expect plausible timelines aligned to project scope and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational framing when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, connect basic science to clinical impact and highlight patient-facing potential or translational steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCSF emphasizes translational impact; explicitly link mechanistic findings to clinical application, and reference clinical resources that enable translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, and inclusion plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plans for diverse cohort recruitment, address health equity in human-subjects research, and consider multi-ancestry inclusion in genomics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame community-engaged research where relevant and describe recruitment strategies and protections to satisfy inclusion expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation framing (novel application + feasible approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame innovation as a novel application or new combination/approach rather than an unsupported claim of being the 'first ever'; acknowledge precedent and cite adapted methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the novelty claim with feasibility; cite the methods you adapt and be honest about prior work to strengthen reviewer trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid investigator overreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not over-promise scope or claim capabilities beyond the team's demonstrated experience or resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match aims to investigator expertise and institutional support; reviewers penalize overreach—scale back scope or add appropriate collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mock-review failure points (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent reviewer criticisms include co-dependent aims, vague Significance, insufficient preliminary data, missing power calculation, absent rigor language, investigator overreach, padded budgets, generic letters, unrealistic timeline, and lack of alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as a checklist to correct weaknesses prior to submission; mock reviews intentionally look for these problems so they can be remediated.
